subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Wear Debris Analysis: Reading the Metal Tea Leaves
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Wear Debris Analysis: Reading the Metal Tea Leaves.

hook.text: Used oil holds tiny metal bits. Each shape tells a story of wear.

buildup.text: Normal wear makes fine dust. Severe wear produces large flakes.

discovery.text: Iron means gears are wearing. Copper means bushings are failing.

twist.text: A sudden spike in particles can warn of failure days before breakdown.

climax.text: Airlines sample engine oil every flight. One bad reading grounds the plane.

punchline.text: The oil remembers every scratch the machine took.

quiz.question: What do copper particles in used oil typically indicate?
options: The oil has oxidized and formed copper compounds
Bronze bushings or copper-alloy parts are wearing abnormally
The oil filter mesh is degrading
